info.title: FetchBox API
info.description:
Self-hosted download manager. Commands over REST, live updates over SSE.

Everything except `/api/health`, `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/auth/*` needs a session: log in with `POST /api/auth/login` (sets the `fetchbox_session` cookie) or send the returned token as `Authorization: Bearer`.

post.summary: Log in and start a session.

429.description: Too many failed attempts (5 per minute); see `Retry-After`

post.summary: End the current session (idempotent) and clear the cookie.
Change the password of an account created in the UI.
post.description: Ends every other session. Not available for a password from the environment or a file.

400.description: New password too short or too long

409.description: The password is managed outside the UI

429.description: Too many failed attempts (5 per minute); see `Retry-After`

post.summary: Create the account on first run and log in.
post.description: Only possible while `setup_required` is true; the code comes from the server log.

200.description: Account created and logged in; sets the `fetchbox_session` cookie

400.description: Password too short or too long

409.description: Setup already done, or authentication is configured externally

429.description: Too many failed attempts (5 per minute); see `Retry-After`

get.summary: Whether login is required and whether the caller is already logged in.

Free space on a disk (by default the one new downloads go to), and how much of it the running
downloads still have to write.

parameters.name: disk
parameters.description:
The disk to look at (a name from `GET /api/disks`; empty = the download directory itself).
Without it: the default disk.

400.description: Not a disk that can be used now (not mounted, or not a folder name)

get.summary:
The disks new downloads can be saved on: the download directory itself and every folder in it
that is a file system of its own (a mounted disk), each with its capacity, and the default one.
Downloads already on the list stay on the disk they were added to.
All downloads, newest first. Running downloads carry live `downloaded` and `speed`.

post.description:
If the URL, the file name or a reserved name collides with something, the server answers
`409` with a `conflict` description and changes nothing. Re-send the request with
`on_conflict` set to `rename` (uses `conflict.suggested_name`) or `overwrite` (replaces the
existing file once the download finishes) to proceed. Not re-sending cancels the add.

400.description: Invalid URL, or overwrite of a name another download is still producing

409.description: Collision; the user must choose (`conflict`), or the SSH server of an `sftp://` address is not trusted yet (`untrusted_host`) or shows another key than the accepted one (`host_key_changed`)

502.description: The remote server could not be reached, or refused the login

507.description: The file does not fit into the free disk space that the running downloads have not claimed. Send the request again with `ignore_space` to add it anyway.

delete.summary:
Remove a download from the list (cancels it first when still active).
A finished file stays on disk unless `delete_file=true`.

parameters.name: delete_file
parameters.description:
Also delete the finished file from the disk. Ignored for downloads that have not
completed (their partial file is always removed).

500.description: The file could not be deleted; the entry is kept so it can be retried

patch.summary:
Change the category of a download, archive it (hide it from the main list) and/or set its own
speed limit.

409.description: Not possible in the download's current status (archiving needs a finished one, a speed limit an unfinished or failed one)

post.summary: Cancel a download and delete its partial file.

Keep the file of a download that is being verified, or that failed its verification, whatever
the checksum says. The download becomes `completed`, without the mark "verified".

409.description: Not being verified and not failed by its verification

post.summary: Pause a queued or running download; offsets are saved so it can resume.
Resume a paused (or retry a failed) download.

get.description:
Each SSE message has an `event:` name (`download`, `progress`, `removed`, `settings`, `torrent`,
`torrent_removed`, `plugin`, `plugin_removed`, `plugin_notice`, or
`resync` with empty data) and a JSON `data:` payload shaped like [`Event`]. After `resync`
(this client fell behind) reload the list with `GET /api/downloads`. Subscribe before
fetching the list so nothing in between is lost.

get.summary: The SSH servers whose host key was accepted, oldest first.

post.summary:
Accept the host key of an SSH server: send the `host`, `port`, `key_type` and `fingerprint`
that a refused `sftp://` request showed, after the user compared the fingerprint with the one
of the server. An earlier key of the same host and port is replaced.

400.description: Not a host, a port and a `SHA256:` fingerprint

delete.summary:
Forget an accepted host key: the server is not trusted any more, and downloads from it stop
until the user accepts its key again.

post.summary:
Look at a URL without adding it: the file name, size, range support and category the server
and the file name suggest. The same checks as an add apply (private addresses can be refused).
A `POST` so that the address, which may carry a token, stays out of access logs.
post.description:
`http(s)://`, `ftp://`, `ftps://` and `sftp://` addresses work. An address of a folder (an FTP
or SFTP directory, or an HTTP directory index) answers with its `entries`. A login for the
source goes in `credentials`; one written into the address is used too and never stored in it.
An SFTP server must be trusted first: the answer is `409` with its fingerprint (see
`POST /known-hosts`).

400.description: Not a usable address (http, https, ftp, ftps or sftp)

409.description: The SSH server of an `sftp://` address is not trusted yet (`untrusted_host`) or shows another key than the accepted one (`host_key_changed`)

502.description: The remote server could not be reached, or refused the login

put.summary:
Replace the settings. Speed limits and `max_concurrent` apply to running downloads
immediately; `connections` applies to downloads started afterwards. `0` speed = unlimited.

get.summary:
A summary of the downloads of a period: how many finished, failed or were cancelled, the data
they fetched, the average and peak speed, the largest file, the categories and the last 14 days.
The numbers outlive the entries of the list: a download that is removed stays in them.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to look (default: everything).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
The caller's distance from UTC in minutes, east positive (`-new Date().getTimezoneOffset()`
in a browser). It decides where a day begins. Default 0 (UTC).

get.summary:
All torrents, newest first. Live numbers (speed, peers, progress) come as `torrent` events on
`/api/events`; this is the state to start from.

post.summary: Add a torrent by magnet link.
post.description:
The torrent shows up at once with the status `metadata`; its name and files arrive from the
swarm, which can take a while (or never happen when nobody has it).

400.description: Not a magnet link, or a tracker at a private address while those are blocked

409.description: The torrent has been added already

502.description: The BitTorrent engine could not start (the port is in use, ...)

post.summary:
Add a torrent from a `.torrent` file: the raw bytes of the file as the request body
(`Content-Type: application/x-bittorrent`), at most 8 MiB.

parameters.name: disk
parameters.description:
Save to this disk (a name from `GET /api/disks`; empty = the download directory itself).
Without it: the default disk for torrents.

400.description: Not a usable .torrent file, or a tracker at a private address while those are blocked

409.description: The torrent has been added already

502.description: The BitTorrent engine could not start

507.description: The files of the torrent do not fit into the free disk space

delete.summary: Remove a torrent from the list; with `delete_files=true` its data goes too.

parameters.name: delete_files
parameters.description: Also delete the downloaded files from the disk.

get.summary:
The files of a torrent and how much of each is on disk. Empty until the description of the
torrent has arrived.

post.summary: Stop a torrent. What it has stays on disk; it stops sending to others too.

get.summary:
The peers of a torrent, with the speed of each. Poll it while a panel is open; it is not part
of the event stream. The list is empty while the torrent is stopped.

post.summary: Start a stopped torrent (or try again after an error).

507.description: What is left does not fit into the free disk space

post.summary:
Let a torrent run although the torrent hours are closed (or keep running when they close). The
exemption ends when the user stops the torrent.

get.summary:
The running version and, unless update checks are switched off in the settings, whether a newer
release has been published on GitHub (looked up at most every six hours and kept meanwhile).

post.summary: Look for a newer release now instead of using the kept answer (not more often than every 30 seconds).

AddRequest.description: Request to add a download by URL.

oneOf.description: Override the category detected from the file name.
Verify the finished file against this checksum (SPEC 6.2.2).

Log in to the source with this user name and password (SPEC 6.12). They win over a login
written into the address (`ftp://user:password@host/file`), which is moved here anyway.

disk.description:
Save to this disk (SPEC 6.14) instead of the default one (`Settings::default_disk`). The
empty name is the download directory itself; leave the field out to take the default.

filename.description: Override the file name suggested by the server.

ignore_space.description:
Add the download even though it does not fit into the free space left after the space
reserved by running downloads (`507` otherwise). The user's call: files may be moved away
or deleted before it starts. If it still does not fit when it starts, it fails then.

start_at.description:
Begin at this moment (unix seconds, at most 31 days ahead) instead of at once. Not together
with `start_now`; it makes no sense with download hours either (they decide the start).

start_now.description: "Download now": do not wait for the download hours, which apply to this download otherwise.

AddTorrentRequest.description:
Add a torrent by magnet link. A `.torrent` file is sent as the raw body of
`POST /api/torrents/file` instead.

disk.description:
Save to this disk (SPEC 6.14) instead of the default one for torrents
(`Settings::torrent_default_disk`, else `default_disk`). Empty = the download directory.

AuthStatus.description: What the UI needs to decide whether to show the login screen.

auth_required.description: A password is configured; unauthenticated requests are refused.

authenticated.description: The caller's session (or the disabled auth) lets it through.

can_change_password.description:
The password was created in the UI and can be changed (`POST /api/auth/password`);
false for a password from `FETCHBOX_PASSWORD` / `--password-file`.

setup_required.description: No account exists yet: show the first-run setup (`POST /api/auth/setup`).

action.description: The action it runs; none just closes the dialog.

closes.description: Close the dialog after the action (default: yes for a button without an action).

Category.description: File category, auto-detected from extension and changeable by the user.

ChecksumAlgo.description: A hash algorithm offered for verification. The common ones that sites publish.

ChecksumInput.description: What the user entered when adding a download: the algorithm and the text they pasted.

value.description:
The checksum as pasted: `d41d8cd9...`, `SHA256: d41d...`, or a line of a checksum file
(`d41d...  name.iso`). Normalised by the server.

ChecksumState.description: A checksum a download is verified against, and what came out of the verification.

actual.description: The digest of the downloaded file when it did not match.

Conflict.description: Description of a collision, shown to the user so they can choose.

existing_id.description: The existing download, when the collision is with one.

existing_modified.description: Unix seconds, for files already on disk.

ConflictBody.description:
`409` body of `POST /downloads` when the new download collides with an existing one.
The UI shows `conflict` and re-sends the request with `on_conflict` set.

ConflictKind.description: Why an add request collided with something.

Credentials.description:
A user name and password for a source that asks for a login (SPEC 6.12). Kept on the server so
that a paused or restarted download can go on; the password is never sent back by the API and
never written to the log.

password.description: May be empty (a login without a password).

DayStat.description: One day of the activity chart.

count.description: Downloads that ended that day, whatever way.

start.description: Unix time of the start of the day (in the client's time zone).

DependencyProgress.description: How far a dependency is on its way.

DependencyView.description: A dependency and whether it is in place.

version.description: The version it was fetched at (a release tag), when it has one.

DiskInfo.description: One place downloads can be saved to, with its space.

name.description: Folder name inside the download directory; empty for the download directory itself.

path.description: Where it is on the machine running FetchBox (shown, never taken from a client).

reserved.description: What the running downloads on this file system still have to write.

total.description: Bytes this program can use on the file system (used plus available).

oneOf.description: A reason to doubt that this is the disk the user meant, if there is one.

DiskSpace.description: Free space on the file system that holds the download directory.

reserved.description:
Bytes reserved by running downloads: what they still have to write on this file system
(size known). Queued, paused and held downloads reserve nothing. New downloads must fit into
`available - reserved`; when `reserved` exceeds `available` (something else filled the disk)
the queue will not fit.

total.description:
Bytes this program can use on the file system: what is used plus what is available
(blocks reserved for root are not counted, like `df`'s `Use%`).

DiskWarning.description:
Why a disk may not be what the user meant (SPEC 6.14). Both are guesses from where the folder is,
shown as a warning: nothing is refused because of them.

Disks.description: The disks FetchBox found and which one new downloads go to by default.

choosable.description: More than the download directory itself can be chosen: the UI offers a choice only then.

default.description: The disk new downloads go to unless the request names another (`Settings::default_disk`).

default_available.description: The default is the download directory or a disk that is mounted now.

disks.description: The download directory first, then the mounted disks by name.

unmounted.description:
Empty folders in the download directory that are not separate disks. A mount point that did
not mount looks like this (an empty folder on the system disk), so they are shown as a hint.

Download.description: A download as stored and shown to the user.

archived.description:
Hidden from the main list (only finished, failed or cancelled downloads can be archived).
The file, if any, stays where it is.

oneOf.description:
The checksum the finished file is verified against (chosen when the download was added),
and what the verification found when it did not match.

disk.description:
The disk the file is saved on (SPEC 6.14): a folder of the download directory, chosen when
the download was added and kept for good, so changing the default disk never moves it.
Empty = the download directory itself.

oneOf.description: Why a queued download is not running (not persisted; set for waiting downloads).

size.description: Total size in bytes, if known.

speed.description: Current speed in bytes/s. Not persisted: filled in for running downloads.

speed_limit.description:
Speed limit of this download alone, bytes/s. Set, it replaces the default per-download
limit of the settings (so it may be higher or lower); `0` means "use the default". The
total limit of all downloads (`Settings::speed_global`) caps the sum either way.

start_at.description: Do not start before this moment (unix seconds): chosen when the download was added.

starts_at.description:
When a waiting download is expected to start (unix seconds): its start time, or the next
opening of the download hours. Not persisted.

subdir.description: Subdirectory of the download directory the file goes to; empty = the directory itself.

username.description:
The user name the download logs in with, if it has a login. The password is kept on the
server and never shown.

verified.description: The file was checked against `checksum` and matched.

waiting_space.description:
Held back because the file does not fit on the disk: it was added on purpose but not
started (status `paused`). Free some space and resume it.

ErrorBody.description: Error body used by every non-2xx response.

oneOf.description: A download was created or its status/metadata changed.
Periodic progress of a running download.
A download was removed from the list.
Settings changed.
A torrent was added, or its status or numbers changed (about once a second while it moves).
A torrent was removed from the list.
A plugin was installed, or its state, settings or dependency progress changed (SPEC 6.15).
A plugin was uninstalled.
A message from a plugin for the user (shown as a toast).

Event.description: Live updates pushed to the UI (SSE).

Field.description: A setting of the plugin, or a field of one of its dialogs.

FieldKind.description: What a settings field or a dialog field is.

FieldView.description: A setting as the interface needs it: the field, and whether it has a value.

has_value.description: Something is stored (also tells a secret was saved).

oneOf.description: The stored value; never set for a `secret`.

Hold.description: Why a queued download is waiting instead of running.

HostKeyBody.description:
`409` body of `POST /downloads` and `POST /probe` when the host key of an SSH server (SFTP) is
not trusted, or is not the accepted one. For an unknown server the UI shows `host_key` (the
fingerprint to compare) and, when the user agrees, sends it to `POST /known-hosts` and asks again.

HostKeyProblem.description: A refused connection to an SSH server because of its host key.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint the server just presented.

HostKeyProblemKind.description: What is wrong with the host key of an SSH server.

InstallMethod.description:
How FetchBox was installed on this machine. The program cannot find that out by itself, so the
installer states it (`FETCHBOX_INSTALL_METHOD`), and the update dialog shows the steps that
belong to it.

KnownHost.description:
An SSH server the user has accepted the host key of (SPEC 6.12). SFTP has no certificate
authorities: the key a server presents is only believed when it is the one that was accepted.

fingerprint.description: `SHA256:` and the unpadded base64 of the key's hash, as `ssh-keygen -l` prints it.

host.description: Host name or address, lowercase, as written in the download address.

LargestFile.description: The biggest file that was downloaded.

ListingEntry.description: One item of a directory index page.

category.description: What the file name says it is (`Other` for a directory).

name.description: Name as shown on the page (decoded), without a trailing slash.

size.description: Size in bytes when the page shows one.

url.description: Absolute address; a file is added with it, a directory is opened with it.

retry_after.description: Seconds until the next attempt is allowed.

LoginResponse.description: Successful login. The same token is also set as the `fetchbox_session` cookie.

token.description: Session token, usable as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Empty when auth is disabled.

NoticeLevel.description: Importance of a message from a plugin.

OnConflict.description: What to do when a new download collides with an existing one (SPEC: name conflicts).

OnHoursEnd.description: What happens to the downloads that are running when the download hours end.

PermissionSummary.description: What a plugin may do, worked out from its manifest and shown before it is installed.

api.description: Parts of FetchBox's API it uses.

download_hosts.description: Where its dependencies are downloaded from.

network.description: Hosts it says it talks to.

process.description: It has a program that runs for as long as it is enabled.

programs.description: Programs it can run (dependencies and files of its own).

runs_downloads.description: It downloads files with its own program instead of FetchBox's engine.

webhook_hosts.description: Where FetchBox sends webhooks on its behalf.

error.description: Why it failed, or what needs a review.

status_text.description: A line the plugin's program reported about itself.

update_available.description: A newer version in the store.

ProbeRequest.description: Request to look at a URL before adding it.

oneOf.description: The login to look at the address with (see `AddRequest::credentials`).

ReleaseNote.description: What a release changed, as its author wrote it on GitHub (Markdown).

body.description: The description of the release (Markdown, shortened when very long). Show it as text.

prerelease.description: A pre-release (`0.7.0-rc.1`); only listed when `Settings::check_prereleases` is on.

Section.description: A group of settings and actions in a plugin's own tab.

Settings.description: Global settings, applied live (SPEC 2, 6.3). Zero speed limit means unlimited.

category_subdirs.description:
Put new downloads into a subdirectory named after their category (`video/`, `music/`, ...).
Existing downloads keep the directory they were created with.

check_prereleases.description:
Also announce pre-releases (`0.7.0-rc.1`) as updates. Off by default: a pre-release is for
those who want to try what is coming and do not mind a rough edge.

check_updates.description:
Ask GitHub now and then whether a newer release exists (`GET /api/version`). Nothing is
sent but the request itself (address of the server, program name and version).

default_disk.description:
The disk new downloads are saved on unless the request names another (SPEC 6.14): a folder
of the download directory that is a file system of its own. Empty = the download directory
itself. Existing downloads stay where they are.

max_concurrent.description: Max simultaneously running downloads; extra ones are `Queued`.

schedule_enabled.description:
Download only during set hours (SPEC 6.3.2): outside them downloads wait, and running ones
are put back in the queue. A single download can opt out (`start_now`).

schedule_from.description: Start of the hours, minutes after local midnight (`0` = 00:00).

schedule_on_end.description: What running downloads do when the download hours end.

schedule_timezone.description:
IANA time zone the hours are in (`Europe/Warsaw`). The server's own clock is usually UTC,
so the zone is stated, not guessed.

schedule_to.description:
End of the hours (exclusive), minutes after local midnight; earlier than the start means
the hours run over midnight (`22:00`-`06:00`).

speed_global.description: Total speed limit of all downloads together, bytes/s.

speed_per_download.description:
Default speed limit of every download, bytes/s. A download with a limit of its own
(`Download::speed_limit`) ignores it.

torrent_default_disk.description:
The disk new torrents are saved on unless the request names another. `None` (the default):
the same disk as the downloads (`default_disk`); `Some("")` is the download directory itself.

torrent_down_limit.description:
Speed limit of all torrents together, receiving, bytes/s (`0` = none). Separate from the
limits of downloads: a swarm and a server are different things to cap.

torrent_schedule_enabled.description:
Let torrents run only during set hours (SPEC 6.3.2). Separate from the download hours: a
swarm is often wanted at other times than a download from a server. Outside the hours a
torrent is stopped, receiving and sending alike, and goes on when they open.

torrent_schedule_from.description: Start of the torrent hours, minutes after local midnight.

torrent_schedule_timezone.description: IANA time zone the torrent hours are in.

torrent_schedule_to.description: End of the torrent hours (exclusive); earlier than the start means over midnight.

torrent_up_limit.description:
Speed limit of all torrents together, sending, bytes/s (`0` = none). Seeding goes on until
the user stops a torrent, so this is what keeps the upload line free.

code.description: One-time code printed in the server log at startup (case and dashes are ignored).

password.description: The new password, at least 8 characters.

ShowIf.description: A field is shown only while another one has this value.

SourceKind.description: What kind of source a download comes from.

SpaceBody.description:
`507` body of `POST /downloads` when the file does not fit. The UI explains the numbers and
offers to add the download anyway (`ignore_space`).

reserved.description:
Part of `free` that the running downloads still have to write. The download fits when
`needed <= free - reserved`.

Stats.description: A summary of the downloads of a period.

active_seconds.description: Seconds spent actually transferring (paused and queued time is not counted).

average_speed.description: Bytes per second over the time spent transferring; `0` when nothing was timed yet.

bytes.description: Bytes fetched by the downloads of the period, plus what unfinished ones have fetched so far.

cancelled.description: Downloads that were cancelled (or removed while unfinished) in the period.

categories.description: Completed downloads per category, biggest first.

completed.description: Downloads that finished successfully in the period.

completed_bytes.description: Total size of the completed files, bytes.

days.description: The last 14 days, oldest first, empty days included (whatever the period).

failed.description: Downloads that failed in the period.

in_progress.description: Downloads that are not finished right now (queued, running, paused). Not tied to the period.

peak_speed.description: The highest speed ever seen, bytes per second (all time, whatever the period).

StatsRange.description: How far back the statistics reach. Days are the user's days (the client sends its UTC offset).

Tab.description: A tab of its own in Settings.

Torrent.description: One torrent as the UI shows it.

disk.description:
The disk it is saved on (SPEC 6.14): a folder of the download directory, chosen when the
torrent was added and kept for good. Empty = the download directory itself.

down_speed.description: Bytes per second from the swarm now.

downloaded.description: Bytes of those files that are on disk and checked.

error.description: Why the torrent stopped (`status` is `error`), or a note such as a full disk.

eta.description: Seconds left at the current speed.

file_count.description: Number of files in the torrent; `0` until the description is known.

finished_at.description: Unix seconds; set when the last byte arrived.

oneOf.description:
Why a torrent that should be running waits: the torrent hours are closed (SPEC 6.3.2).
Computed, not stored; the status is `paused` meanwhile.

info_hash.description: The identity of the torrent: 40 hexadecimal characters (SHA-1 of its `info` dictionary).

magnet.description: The magnet link the torrent was added with; none for a `.torrent` file.

name.description:
The name inside the torrent; the name from the magnet link (or the hash) until the
description has arrived.

peers_connecting.description: Peers we are trying to connect to.

peers_known.description: Peers heard of (from trackers, DHT, other peers), connected or not.

size.description: Total size of the files that are wanted; `None` until the description is known.

start_now.description: The torrent hours do not apply to this torrent ("Start now").

starts_at.description: Unix seconds when the torrent hours open next (only with `hold`).

up_speed.description: Bytes per second to the swarm now.

uploaded.description: Bytes sent to other peers, over all runs of the program.

downloaded.description: Bytes of this file that are on disk and checked.

client.description: The program the peer runs, as it names itself (`qBittorrent 5.0`).

down_speed.description: Bytes per second from this peer now.

downloaded.description: Bytes received from this peer since it was first connected.

oneOf.description: How the connection is made (only for a connected peer).

up_speed.description: Bytes per second to this peer now.

TorrentPeers.description: The peers of a torrent, with the counts of every state.

peers.description:
Connected peers first (fastest first), then those being connected, then the rest; at most
[`MAX_PEERS_LISTED`].

truncated.description: The list was cut at the limit.

TorrentStatus.description:
What a torrent is doing now, in the words a BitTorrent client uses.

The engine only knows "initialising", "live", "paused" and "error"; the rest is read from the
numbers (peers, progress) by [`TorrentStatus::derive`].

TrustHost.description: Request to accept the host key of an SSH server: send back what a refused add showed.

archived.description:
Hide the download from the main list (`true`) or bring it back (`false`). Only finished,
failed or cancelled downloads can be archived (`409` otherwise).

oneOf.description: New category (manual override of the detected one).

speed_limit.description:
Speed of this download alone, bytes per second. It replaces the default speed of each
download (it may be faster or slower); `0` removes it, so the default applies again. The
total limit of all downloads still caps the sum. Only for queued, running, paused and
failed downloads (`409` otherwise). Applied live to a running download.

start_now.description:
`true`: "download now". The download hours no longer apply to this download and a start
time it was given is dropped, so a download that waits starts at once and a running one is
not stopped when the hours close. Only for queued and running downloads (`409` otherwise).

UrlInfo.description: What the remote server says about a URL: what an add request would work with.

category.description: Category the download would get when none is chosen.

entries.description: For a listing: the directories first, then the files, each group in page order. Empty for a file.

filename.description: The (sanitized) file name the download would get.

resumable.description: The server honours `Range`, so the download can be paused and resumed.

size.description: Size in bytes; `None` when the server does not tell.

truncated.description: The page had more items than are returned.

UrlKind.description: What a URL turned out to be.

VersionInfo.description: The version of the running program and what is known about newer ones.

check_failed.description: The last attempt did not get an answer (offline, rate limited, ...).

checked_at.description: When the answer was obtained (unix seconds); `None` if no check has succeeded yet.

enabled.description: Update checks are switched on (`Settings::check_updates`). When off, nothing else is set.

oneOf.description:
How this copy was installed (`FETCHBOX_INSTALL_METHOD`); `None` when nobody said. Decides
which update steps the UI shows.

latest.description: Version of the newest published release, without a leading `v`.

latest_prerelease.description: `latest` is a pre-release (only possible when `Settings::check_prereleases` is on).

notes.description: What changed in every release newer than `current`, newest first (at most ten).
